scope: Define divergence by integration by parts, parallel to the gradient characterization, replacing the deformation/determinant derivation.
prose_status: proof-draft; edited at Steven’s request; further review pending
changes: Divergence is defined as the unique continuous real function satisfying the integral identity against every real smooth compactly supported test function.
The right side is first written using the metric gradient, then explained as the directional derivative of the test function.
Coordinate integration by parts proves existence and derives the weighted-density formula; a test function supported where a continuous difference has one sign proves uniqueness.
The correction -2Q/y is derived from the hyperbolic area density. The deformation F_t, its determinant and little-o notation are removed.
The notation index and Compare now use the integral characterization. Labels, numbering and the subsequent Laplacian/isometry proofs are retained.

formalization_impact.remaining: Define the weighted measure and differentiable vector-field interface, prove the integral characterization and pointwise uniqueness, then connect divergence to the gradient and analytic Laplacian. No coordinate-only proxy is claimed as this formalization.
mathlib_dependency_inspection: Mathlib.Analysis.Distribution.AEEqOfIntegralContDiff: IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero supplies almost-everywhere uniqueness on an open subset after establishing local integrability and the test-function identity; continuity and positivity of the area density must still yield pointwise uniqueness.

Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts supplies directional/Fréchet integration-by-parts lemmas for additive Haar measure. Application requires localization to compact test supports and the density conversion; hyperbolic area itself is not additive Haar measure.
